reviewer: Luna high independent adversarial source review

findings.claim: task_to_domain returns Result<Issue, IssueError>, but update_issue returns Ok(task_to_domain(...)) without ?, producing Result<Result<Issue, IssueError>, IssueError> where the BoxFuture requires Result<Issue, IssueError>.
findings.repair: Propagate the conversion error exactly as create_issue and get_issue do (or otherwise return the conversion Result directly), then recheck all changed provider conversion call sites before compilation.

findings.claim: A response-controlled workflow state id is inserted raw into the follow-up issueUpdate GraphQL document. A provider response containing a quote, backslash, or GraphQL punctuation can alter the mutation sent with the Linear authorization; user title/id values are escaped but StateNode.id is not.
findings.repair: Use a GraphQL variable for stateId, or validate and escape the returned id before constructing the mutation. Add a response-injection fixture that proves no injected field reaches the second request.

findings.claim: create_issue invokes gh issue create without a repository flag and only validates the printed URL after the create side effect. It derives expected_host from GH_HOST, while configured extra_flags are explicitly list-only. A cwd/host mismatch can therefore create in an unintended repository or create successfully and then return a parse error; the comment claiming it never resolves against cwd is false.
findings.repair: Bind creation to an admitted repository/worktree authority before invoking gh, or document and test the existing cwd contract with an explicit preflight. At minimum keep creation and follow-up authority consistent and add a fake gh argv/cwd fixture; do not rely on post-create URL validation to prevent the side effect.

findings.claim: Linear converts provider-returned identifier and URL into an Issue before validating them. Router callers later validate the Issue before cache/UI use, but the public Linear backend itself can return a malformed domain object and direct backend consumers bypass the required adapter boundary.
findings.repair: Make the Linear conversion fallible and validate the identifier/number/public URL before constructing the domain object, consistently with Jira and Kaneo.

findings.claim: PluginIssueBackend::new changed from returning Self to Result<Self, IssueError>, and IssueRouter::push_backend changed from returning () to Result<(), IssueError>. Both are public methods, so downstream Rust callers using the pre-change signatures no longer compile. IssueError also gained enum variants, which affects exhaustive downstream matches.
findings.repair: Preserve the existing public constructors and add fallible try_new/try_push seams, or explicitly version/document the intentional breaking API change before landing. The approved scope calls for preserving public compatibility.

validated_areas: TrackerHttpClient keeps configured scheme/host/effective port/base path, refuses redirects and nonidentity encoding, enforces bounded request/response bodies, and carries one permit/deadline through provider operations in source inspection.

Jira and Kaneo REST route construction is structurally encoded and checks provider ids before path use; Linear user id/title/query interpolation is escaped or variable-backed except for the returned state id above.
Control client/server issue identity round-trip tests exercise one complete encoded segment, malformed ids have zero ControlApi calls, and plugin opaque keys retain delimiter/Unicode behavior.
Router validates returned issue identity before cache/list/search aggregation, while the Linear adapter ordering remains a direct-consumer gap described above.
The d96 follow-up only tightens fixture signal assertions and cancellation joins relative to 7ef; it does not resolve the production blockers.
